preamble: No verified direct case of /ʃ/ > ∅ has been found. The previously cited Ancient Greek development (genesis vs. geneos) concerns Proto-Greek intervocalic /s/, which debuccalized to /h/ and was then lost (*génes-os > génehos > géneos 'of a race'); no /ʃ/ is involved. That change belongs to the s_to_h and h_to_empty cells.

examples.from: Proto-Greek *génes-os 'of a race, of a kind'
examples.note: The deleted sound was /s/ via /h/, not /ʃ/

sources: Sihler, A. L. (1995). New Comparative Grammar of Greek and Latin. Oxford University Press. https://global.oup.com/academic/product/new-comparative-grammar-of-greek-and-latin-9780195083453
